Comparative data from congeneric species suggest that this oxygen consumption value is near the predicted scaling relationship for bats of this body mass, though direct intraspecific comparisons remain limited. The stable thermal environment maintained during these measurements is critical for obtaining reliable baseline values, as fluctuations in body temperature can substantially alter resting metabolic rates. Field studies have shown that free-ranging individuals may exhibit lower metabolic rates during periods of resource scarcity, highlighting the plasticity inherent in the species’ energy budget.
